## Answer: 807

**Reduction.** Write $cm = 2^a5^b n$ with $\gcd(n,10)=1$. The fraction $(10^t-1)/(cm)$ is short iff $n \mid 10^t-1$, i.e. $\operatorname{ord}_n(10) \mid t$. The condition that no smaller $k$ works forces $t = \operatorname{ord}_n(10)$ (with $\operatorname{ord}_1(10)=1$). So
$$S(m)=\{\operatorname{ord}_{n_c}(10): 1\le c\le 2017\},\qquad n_c=\text{the part of } cm \text{ coprime to } 10.$$

**Upper bound.** Since $n_c$ depends only on $c$ with its factors of 2 and 5 removed, it depends only on $d=c'\in D$, where $D$ is the set of integers in $[1,2017]$ coprime to 10. Thus $|S(m)|\le |D|$. Counting: $[1,2000]$ contains $800$ such integers, and $[2001,2017]$ contributes $2001,2003,2007,2009,2011,2013,2017$ (7 more). So $|D|=807$.

**Achieving 807.** Let $m' = \prod_{q\le 2017,\ q\ne 2,5} q^{K_q}$ over primes $q$, with each $K_q$ very large, and let $m=m'$. For $d=\prod q^{e_q}\in D$, $n_d = m'd$, and
$$V(d)=\operatorname{ord}_{m'd}(10)=\operatorname{lcm}_q \operatorname{ord}_{q^{K_q+e_q}}(10).$$
The exponent of $q$ in $\operatorname{ord}_{q^N}(10)$ equals $N$ plus a bounded constant. Contributions from the other prime powers have bounded $q$-adic valuation. Since $K_q$ is much larger than these bounds, $v_q(V(d)) = K_q + e_q + c_q$ with $c_q$ independent of $d$. So $V(d)$ determines every $e_q$, hence determines $d$. Therefore the 807 values $V(d)$ are distinct, and $|S(m)|=807$.

Hence the maximum is $807$.

ANSWER: 807
